title: The Culiacán Clinic That Opened in 2003 With Three Services
conflicts: Founder confirmed as Jesús Vizcarra Calderón (wife Alma Avendaño de Vizcarra first president). His son's illness: brain tumour at four, 25 years earlier (Vizcarra to El Financiero 2024; CEO to Expansión 2025) versus a stroke about 36 years earlier (Vizcarra to Sabina Berman, 2026); the story gives both, attributed, undated. Founding date October 2003 (Expansión, Telediario, Tus Buenas Noticias) versus October 2002 (SDP Noticias column) and 'end of 2014' (Forbes México, an error); October 2003 used. Clinic counts for mid-2024 differ (218-222 Publimetro, 235 El Financiero) and patient figures differ (18 million a year in 2024; 23 million in 2026; 'almost 3 million a month' in 2025); the story uses 'more than 200 clinics' and 'more than 18 million patients a year' for 2024, where two sources agree. Forbes says it received IDB loans; Expansión quotes the CEO saying the board declined one; not used.
notes: Editor should know: an SDP Noticias opinion column repeats hearsay that Vizcarra is a compadre of the cartel figure 'El Mayo' Zambada and voices rival laboratories' complaints about Salud Digna's non-profit tax status; unsubstantiated in the other reporting, not part of the episode and not mentioned in the edition. Spanish quotations are paraphrased; the only direct quotation is the English motto from the 2011 release. Strong diagnostics link, but talQen is not mentioned, per the group instruction.
